description: This topic provides the numerical value of the likelihood of an uncertain event occurring. In competitive exams, questions based on coins, dice, and playing cards are primarily asked under this section.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Introduction to the fundamental terms and definitions required to understand probability theory.

key_concepts.explanation: An experiment where all possible outcomes are known in advance, but the exact outcome of a specific trial cannot be predicted.
The set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment is called the sample space.
Any subset of the sample space is considered an event.

sections.title: Types of Events
sections.description: Classification of different types of events that are important for solving problems.

key_concepts.explanation: Events that cannot occur simultaneously. If one event happens, the other cannot.
When the occurrence of one event does not affect the probability of the occurrence of another event.
The event representing the non-occurrence of event 'E' is called a complementary event.

sections.title: Steps to Find Probability
sections.description: Standard procedure to solve any probability problem in a step-by-step manner.

steps.title: Total Possible Outcomes
steps.detail: First, find the total number of elements in the sample space n(S) for the given random experiment.

steps.title: Favorable Outcomes
steps.detail: Calculate the number of outcomes n(E) that favor the specific event asked in the question.

steps.title: Application of Formula
steps.detail: Substitute the values into the main formula P(E) = n(E) / n(S) to find the required probability.

sections.title: Laws of Probability
sections.description: Important mathematical rules for finding the probability of compound and conditional events.

equations: P(A U B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)
